I'm checking the first candidate, "Myotonic dystrophy" at the start of the text, and asking whether it counts as a specific disease or a broader disease class. Myotonic dystrophy has subtypes like DM1 and DM2, so it could be read as a family, but I'm recalling that the NCBI disease corpus typically annotates it as a specific disease.

Myotonic dystrophy counts as a specific disease here, since its MeSH entry is one disease with types 1 and 2. The second mention of it is a duplicate and gets the same label. The "DM" abbreviation also stands for myotonic dystrophy and gets the same label, but as its own annotation.

I'm working through the remaining checks: the "DM phenotype" use is a modifier, since DM describes the noun phenotype, and the title's "Myotonic dystrophy" stays a specific disease. The bare "disease" in "disease pathogenesis" is a general term I won't annotate, and the output should be a single line of JSON without markdown.

content.text: {"decisions":[{"id":1,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"'Myotonic dystrophy' names one specific disease (DM) with a single definition in the title, so it is a Specific Disease rather than a class.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions"},{"id":2,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"Repeated mention of 'Myotonic dystrophy' in the abstract refers to the same specific disease; duplicate mentions are annotated separately.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 4: Annotate duplicate mentions"},{"id":3,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"'DM' is the abbreviation defining Myotonic dystrophy and is used as a separate synonymous mention for the specific disease.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 6: Annotate all synonymous mentions"},{"id":4,"entity":"DiseaseClass","rationale":"'muscular dystrophy' refers to a family of multiple specific diseases (the most common form of a class of muscle disorders), so it is a Disease Class.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1: Disease Class definition"},{"id":5,"entity":"CompositeMention","rationale":"'myotonia and myopathy' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases, so it is annotated as one Composite Mention.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 2: Contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)"},{"id":6,"entity":"Modifier","rationale":"'DM' in 'a DM phenotype' is a disease abbreviation used to modify the noun 'phenotype', so it is annotated as a Modifier.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers"},{"id":7,"entity":"NONE","rationale":"'disease' is a very general term that is excluded from annotation, even when used in 'disease pathogenesis'.","guideline_section":"What NOT to Annotate 4: Do not annotate general terms"}]}
